note: Attacker-controlled input buffer length is captured as `end`; this is the starting point for all subsequent address calculations.
Only checks that the buffer has at least 3 bytes, but does not account for the root width bytes needed before the root data address.
Reads the root width from the last byte; attacker controls this value to select W8 (1 byte), W16 (2 bytes), W32 (4 bytes), or W64 (8 bytes).
Reads the root type and element width from the second-to-last byte; attacker controls this to set the root type to a reference type (e.g., String, Blob, Map, Vector, Key).
Computes the root data address as `end - 2 - root_width.n_bytes()`. With a small buffer and W8 root width, this can place the address at or near the end of the buffer.

code: if fxb_type.is_reference() { address = deref_offset(&buffer, address, parent_width)?; }
note: For reference types, the address is dereferenced by reading an offset at the current address and subtracting it; this can move the address to any position within the buffer.
Calls read_usize which for W8 directly indexes `buffer[address..][0]` without bounds checking; if address equals buffer length, this panics with index out of bounds.
Creates a slice starting at the attacker-controlled address; if address exceeds the buffer length, this panics immediately.

Off-by-one error: for W8, directly indexes cursor[0] without checking that the slice is non-empty. When address == buffer.len(), cursor is empty and this panics with index out of bounds, causing a crash.
